compiled_state.description:
## Symptom

Three tests fail intermittently in `make verify` and in CI, in different combinations each
run. Observed in a full `make verify` at `origin/main`:

```
FAILED tests/interfaces/facades/test_plan_review_attestation_facades.py::test_cli_passed_but_unsigned_is_exit_11_with_byte_identical_stderr
FAILED tests/interfaces/facades/test_verify_completion_facades.py::test_cli_llm_error_is_clean_exit_one
3 failed, 20648 passed, 27 skipped in 8293.97s
```

Each passes when run alone. The failure is produced by test ORDER, not by any one test.

## Reproduction (deterministic)

Run the two facade tests in that order, on a clean `origin/main` tree:

```
pytest tests/interfaces/facades/test_plan_review_attestation_facades.py::test_cli_passed_but_unsigned_is_exit_11_with_byte_identical_stderr \
       tests/interfaces/facades/test_verify_completion_facades.py::test_cli_llm_error_is_clean_exit_one \
       -p no:randomly -p no:cacheprovider
```

The second fails. Reversing or isolating them passes. Reproduced at `7c3cb5e9a4f`.

## Root cause

`src/rebar/_logging.py:81` constructs the handler as
`logging.StreamHandler(sys.stderr)`, which binds the stream OBJECT at construction time.
`install_stderr_handler` is deliberately idempotent (`_HANDLER_MARKER`, `:74-77`): once a
handler is installed on the `rebar` logger, every later call returns early and the original
handler — with its original stream — stays for the life of the process.

That is correct for production, where a process has one stderr for its lifetime. It is wrong
whenever `sys.stderr` is REPLACED mid-process. Under pytest, `capsys` swaps `sys.stderr` per
test and closes the buffer at teardown. So:

1. The first test to call `main()` installs a handler bound to THAT test's capsys buffer.
2. The test ends; pytest closes the buffer.
3. A later test calls `main()`. The marker short-circuits the install, so the stale handler
   survives.
4. `rebar._commands._seam:357` emits its "authorship: signing SKIPPED" warning. The handler
   writes to the closed buffer:

```
--- Logging error ---
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../logging/__init__.py", line 1163, in emit
    stream.write(msg + self.terminator)
ValueError: I/O operation on closed file.
```

5. `logging` prints that report to the CURRENT `sys.stderr`, which the later test is
   capturing. Its assertion `"Traceback" not in err` therefore fails on a traceback that
   belongs to the logging subsystem, not to the command under test.

Which tests collide depends on which one calls `main()` first, so under `-n 4 --dist
worksteal` the failing set varies run to run. That is the intermittency.

This is not a test-only defect. Any embedder that redirects `sys.stderr` after the first
rebar entrypoint call — a library consumer, a wrapping CLI, a captured subprocess harness —
keeps writing to the original stream.

## The fix

Resolve `sys.stderr` at EMIT time instead of binding it at construction. The idempotency
marker stays (it exists to stop duplicate handlers stacking, and that is still wanted); what
changes is that the one installed handler stops pinning a stream that can die underneath it.

This deletes the failure class rather than reordering or isolating the tests, and adds no
mechanism of any ratcheted kind — it is a handler that reads a global at emit time instead of
at construction.

## Not the fix

- Marking the tests as order-dependent, or pinning their order. That hides an observable
  defect in the shipped logging path.
- Resetting handlers in a fixture. That is a new `autouse_fixture` — a ratcheted mechanism
  kind — installed to work around a library bug, and it would leave the embedder case broken.
- `recheck` in CI. The project rule is explicit: a flaky test is a bug to root-cause, never a
  retry.

## The third failure

`tests/unit/test_fetch_common_dir_coordination.py::test_uncoordinated_parallel_fetches_can_race_but_coordination_prevents_it`
also failed in the same run. It has not been diagnosed yet and may be an unrelated race.
Triage it separately before assuming it shares this cause.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The reproduction above passes: the two facade tests pass when run in that order, on
      that command line.
- [ ] Each of the two still passes when run alone, and the full
      `tests/interfaces/facades/` directory passes.
- [ ] A regression test fails without the fix and passes with it, asserting that a warning
      emitted after `sys.stderr` is replaced reaches the NEW stream — not that the tests
      happen to pass in some order.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_fetch_common_dir_coordination.py::test_uncoordinated_parallel_fetches_can_race_but_coordination_prevents_it`
      is diagnosed: either fixed here, or filed as its own bug with evidence that it is a
      different cause.
- [ ] No new `autouse_fixture`, `env_var`, `config_key`, `feature_flag`, `ci_gate`, `lock` or
      `test_helper` is added; `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exits 0.
- [ ] `make verify` passes.

## Provider neutrality

No model, vendor, CI provider or harness is involved. `_logging.py` is in-process and reads
no CI environment, so the fix behaves identically under any CI provider or none.
compiled_state.title: Stale stderr handler makes CLI facade tests order-dependent
